description: The site_onscene_information report states the accident site elevation as 'about 2,465 ft', while the meteorology_report states the accident site elevation as 'about 2,500 ft'. These are not contradictions: each document derives elevation from a different source (on-scene GPS survey vs. NWS gridded terrain data), and both hedge with 'about'. The 35-ft difference is within normal inter-source measurement variability for remote terrain.

The dispatch_sheet records 'Fuel On Board: Unknown as of 3/22/19 13:00', reflecting genuine operational uncertainty at the time of dispatch. The weight_balance_information document reconstructs 38 gallons of fuel at Airport-Charlie departure, based on post-accident analysis of fueling records and flight history. The apparent discrepancy is a legitimate preliminary-vs-final distinction: the dispatch record captures real-time uncertainty while the W&B reconstruction is an investigative estimate.
